# Zhex

> Zhex is a Forth-inspired programming language for builders, built on small words and big ideas: you build the vocabulary you program with, and every word you write extends the language. Compact code with visible flow, meaningful names, and checked types, executed by a working Go interpreter. Every program is checked — names, types, and word connections — before any of it runs.

## Docs

- [Manifesto](https://desireco.github.io/zhex/manifesto.html): the intentions behind Zhex — visible data, small composed words, a language machines can read, errors that teach, performance you can measure, and code humans enjoy reviewing. Full text at docs/manifesto.md; concrete goals at docs/language-goals.md.
- [Docs](https://desireco.github.io/zhex/docs/tldr.html): the TL;DR-first guide — Zhex in a minute, then topic pages for language concepts, the standard library, and tools.
- [Getting started](https://desireco.github.io/zhex/docs/getting-started.html): install and run a first program.
- Agent workflow: write the program, then run `zhex run file.zhex --report=json` — checking happens before execution, so a clean run means names, types, and word connections resolved. Read each report entry `{code, severity, file, line, column, message, hint}` and fix what it names; the hint states the action, and human-readable diagnostics show the source line with a caret under the whole failing expression. Rerun until clean. To watch what a program did instead, add `--trace` — JSONL step events stream to stderr before any diagnostic, tracing never fails a run, and the flags combine (events, then the report). To compile a checked program to a standalone WebAssembly module instead of interpreting it, run `zhex compile file.zhex [-o out.wasm] [--target=browser|wasi]` (browser is the default); assembling needs the free wasm-tools tool — install it with `cargo install wasm-tools`, `pacman -S wasm-tools`, or `brew install wasm-tools` (a release binary from the BytecodeAlliance releases page also works), and without it the coded `missing-tool` diagnostic prints those three install lines. A construct the compiler does not cover yet fails the compile with `not-available-in-build` naming the construct — run that program with `zhex run` instead. Explore interactively by piping entries to `zhex repl` standard input — words and values persist across entries, `words` lists effective signatures, and an error prints its diagnostic while the session survives. Take example code and output from the examples page — both come from the actual interpreter.
- [Language](https://desireco.github.io/zhex/docs/syntax.html): syntax, values, words, flows, control flow, Results, and modules.
- What Zhex does not have: no method syntax — a dot qualifies a word name (`text.upper(s)`) or reads a record field (`customer.name`), never a method call; no lambda or anonymous functions — callbacks are named words or partials built from `_` holes; no generic words or records — only choices and `Option<T>` take a type parameter; no iterator or lazy-sequence values — iteration exists only as `for ... in` loops (range, list, array, map, file.stream) and `while`; no string interpolation — concatenate with `+` (a String and an Int concatenate; two Ints add) and convert with `int.to-string`; no exceptions — failures are `Result` values handled with postfix `try` or `catch` at every caller; no `break`, `continue`, or early `return` — a word's value is its final expression, and an `if`, `match`, or `flow` block can supply it conditionally; chained branches use `elif`; no null — absence is `Option.None`; no implicit conversions except the string-context Int for `+` and `print`; no compound assignment — write `count = count + 1`; conditions must be `Bool`, never numbers or strings.
- Block values: `if`, `match`, and `flow` can be the entire right-hand side of a `let`, `var`, or assignment; the block's final value is used. They are not general nested expressions or call arguments.
- While loops: `while condition` repeats an indented body while its `Bool` condition holds, evaluated before each pass. It is a statement of type `Unit` — never a binding or assignment right-hand side — with no `break`/`continue`; it may run forever by design with no iteration limit, and the word-call depth limit does not apply to loop iterations.
- Multiline syntax: expressions may continue inside `()`, `[]`, and `{}`; blank and comment-only lines are allowed while a delimiter is open. Trailing commas are rejected, and `<...>` type arguments do not open a continuation.
- Word doc comments: a contiguous block of full-line `##` comments at column 1 directly above a `word` declaration becomes that word's doc — one optional leading space is stripped per line, lines join with newlines, a blank line or plain `#` comment between the block and `word` detaches it, and `##` anywhere else stays a plain comment (`###` reads as `##` plus text). User words only: entry-file words, module words (`words` lists them qualified, e.g. `math.gcd(...)`), and REPL definitions; records, choices, and built-ins get none. `words` prints the doc indented four spaces beneath the signature, a blank doc line as an empty line; docs live on the word, so a redefinition replaces the doc and a doc-less redefinition clears it without affecting signature compatibility. In the REPL, a comment-only line never completes an entry — it joins the next line's entry (a `##` doc block shares its entry with the word it documents), and `words` typed right after a comment line still runs the command.
- Simple word calls and partials: parenthesized calls remain valid; a simple call may omit call parentheses at a complete statement, binding/assignment right-hand side, final word value, or flow step. Commas separate arguments (`add 1, 2`); whitespace alone does not. `print 1 + 1` passes one arithmetic result. Keep nested calls parenthesized (`print(add(1, 2))`) and use parentheses for negative or list-literal first arguments; `values [0]` remains indexing. A bare word name at a complete expression boundary calls an accessible zero-argument word, while a same-named value binding is a value. A flow step receives the current value as its first argument, then any comma-separated extra arguments. A trailing `try` or `catch` guards the whole bare call; use parentheses to place `try` on a fallible argument separately. A standalone `_` slot creates an explicit function value with required parameters in hole order. Supported built-ins and user words can be partially applied; overloaded built-ins need an annotation or sufficient call-site constraints, while constructors, loop-only operations, `error.set-reporter`, `console.exit`, and `console.fail` are excluded. Captured arguments evaluate once in source order at creation; defaults remain deferred until invocation. A fallible target's function type includes `Result` in its return and fails only when invoked; a capture-argument `try` happens at creation. Function values have monomorphic arrow types such as `(Int) -> Int` and do not enable automatic currying.
- [Calls and defaults](https://desireco.github.io/zhex/docs/calls.html): simple comma-separated word-call syntax, zero-argument calls, flow arguments, and boundaries where parentheses remain necessary.
- [Records and named types](https://desireco.github.io/zhex/docs/records.html): nominal record declarations, positional or named construction, field defaults, immutable fields, and explicit type annotations.
- [Choices and matching](https://desireco.github.io/zhex/docs/choices.html): concrete named alternatives, payload binding, exhaustive cases, and a final `case _` default.
- [Lists and arrays](https://desireco.github.io/zhex/docs/collections.html): homogeneous shared collections, checked indexing, resizing, limits, and failure handling.
- [Maps](https://desireco.github.io/zhex/docs/maps.html): typed inferred keys and values, `Option` lookup, insertion-ordered iteration, updates, and flows.
- [Dates and time zones](https://desireco.github.io/zhex/docs/temporal.html): calendar dates, elapsed durations, instants, named IANA zones, and DST-aware operations.
- [JSON](https://desireco.github.io/zhex/docs/json.html): typed JSON decoding with record defaults, strict validation and field paths, and encoding of supported values.
- [XML](https://desireco.github.io/zhex/docs/xml.html): typed XML decoding with attribute fields, repeated-element lists, strict validation, element paths, and the common Error family.
- [Collection iteration](https://desireco.github.io/zhex/docs/iteration.html): list indices, array coordinates, row-major arrays, insertion-ordered map traversal, and mutation guards.
- Rich-value rules: record declarations and choices are nominal. Record constructors accept all-positional arguments in field order or all-named arguments in any field order; the forms cannot mix. Trailing defaults may be omitted, and evaluate after supplied arguments in declaration order. Named arguments apply only to record constructors, not words, built-ins, or choice alternatives. `type Names = alias List<String>` defines a transparent alias. Fields are immutable; choice alternatives are constructed by qualified name, with payloads in declared order. A choice may have one type parameter: payload constructors infer it, while a nullary alternative needs an expected type. Generic records and words are not supported. Match every alternative once, or use one final `case _`; a default after all named alternatives is an error. Choices cannot be printed or compared directly, payloads cannot contain `Result`, and caught concrete errors need `error.wrap` before storing in an `Error` payload. Lists infer homogeneous elements; empty list values need an expected `List<T>`. Arrays use explicit `List<Int>` shapes, rank 2..32, and at most 1,000,000 elements. List/array reads, `array.new`, `list.append`, and `array.resize` return ordinary values and diagnose invalid operations at runtime; direct `try` or `catch` selects a checked Result for that operation only. Plain indexed writes return `Unit` and raise runtime diagnostics for invalid rank, bounds, or active-iteration mutation; parenthesized indexed writes return a checked `Result<Unit, Error>`. `Map<K, V>` infers types from nonempty literals; empty maps need an expected type. Map literal keys are constant `String`, `Int`, or `Bool` literals; dynamic keys are allowed for lookup, update, containment, and removal. Lookup yields `Option<V>` without `try`, and map values cannot contain `Result`. Map iteration preserves insertion order. Mutation of an actively traversed map raises a runtime `collection-iterating` diagnostic before changing storage; it is not a `Result`. Collection aliases share storage. Caught concrete errors may go directly to built-in `error.*` operations, but require `error.wrap` before passing to a user word expecting `Error` or storing in an Error-typed record field or collection; flow cannot pass Error values to user-defined steps.
- [Standard library](https://desireco.github.io/zhex/docs/text.html): text, buffers, files, and console operations.
- JSON: `json.decode(raw, defaults)` infers the target from a typed default and returns `Result<T, Error>`; missing record fields use defaults, invalid supplied fields do not. Present Lists/Maps replace defaults, and each decoded value gets fresh copies of mutable defaults while aliases inside that value remain shared. `json.encode(value)` returns compact JSON; record fields follow declaration order and Map keys follow insertion order. Supported types are `Int`, `Bool`, `String`, records, `List<T>`, `Map<String, T>`, and `Option<T>` in nested combinations, except direct nested `Option<Option<T>>`; `null` means `Option.None`. Int accepts signed 64-bit integer-form JSON tokens only; decimal/exponent notation and overflow reject. `json.parse(raw)` returns `Result<Json, Error>` — a host-predeclared recursive tree type `Json` with constructors `Json.Null`, `Json.Bool(value)`, `Json.Text(value)`, `Json.Number(literal: String)`, `Json.List(values: List<Json>)`, and `Json.Object(fields: Map<String, Json>)`; trees are ordinary data (constructible, storable in records, matched with plain `match`) and `json.encode(tree)` accepts them: `encode(parse(raw))` preserves key order and number literals byte-for-byte and normalizes whitespace to compact; `Json.Number` literals are validated against the JSON number grammar at encode (`json-type` plus a JSON Pointer path), `text.to-int` converts when an Int is wanted, and map lookup distinguishes `Option.Some(Json.Null)` from `Option.None`; recursion stays host-only (a user record may hold a `Json` field), JSON depth and word-call depth are both 256 so a recursive word over a maximally deep tree sits exactly at the call-depth edge. Arrays, resources, Results, non-Option choices, and non-string-key maps are unsupported. JSON errors include `json-syntax`, `json-type`, `json-field`, `json-range`, and `json-depth`; `error.detail(error, "path")` is an RFC 6901 JSON Pointer, with root as empty string and `~`/`/` escaped as `~0`/`~1`.
- XML: `xml.decode(text, defaults)` infers the target from a typed default and returns `Result<T, Error>`, schema-directed exactly like `json.decode` (same supported types: `Int`, `Bool`, `String`, records, `List<T>`, `Map<String, T>`, `Option<T>` in nested combinations, except direct nested `Option<Option<T>>`). Mapping: element attributes map onto same-named record fields verbatim alongside child-element fields, and an attribute name colliding with a child element name fails the decode; repeated same-named child elements collect into a `List<T>` field in document order; an absent element or attribute falls back to its default (so `Option.None` default plus absence yields `Option.None`, and a present element yields `Option.Some`); text-only elements decode as `String` or `Int` (`Bool` accepts exactly `true`/`false`); for a `List` or `Map` target the element children are the items, keyed by child element name for maps. Strictness: unknown elements and attributes fail, duplicate non-list elements fail, missing required fields without defaults fail, mixed content (non-whitespace text next to child elements) fails, namespace-prefixed or namespace-resolved names fail (including a default `xmlns`), DTD/entity declarations and undefined entities fail, and malformed XML fails — all before any substitution. Entities: the five predefined (`&amp;` `&lt;` `&gt;` `&quot;` `&apos;`) and numeric character references decode; nothing is fetched, ever. Limits: nesting depth 256, one million elements. Errors are the common `Error` family with stable codes `xml-syntax`, `xml-type`, `xml-field`, `xml-range`, and `xml-depth`; `error.detail(error, "path")` carries the element path (`/server/endpoints/0/host`, root as empty string), plus `reason` (`unknown`, `duplicate`, `missing`, `collision`, `prefixed`), `expected`/`actual`, and `offset`/`line`/`column` for syntax failures.
- [Tools](https://desireco.github.io/zhex/docs/repl.html): the REPL, diagnostics, compiling to WebAssembly, and editor support.
- Vocabulary: text work uses the `text.*` words — `length` (code points), `line-count`, `word-count`, `upper`, `lower`, `trim`, `contains`, `index-of` (code-point position, `-1` when absent), `slice(start, end)` (code points, bounds clamp, `start >= end` is empty), `replace(old, new)` (every occurrence, literal, empty `old` errors), `split(separator)` (literal, preserves empty fields, no trim, empty separator yields code points, fails `collection-limit` past one million elements), `join(separator)` (between elements, empty list is empty text), `starts-with(prefix)` and `ends-with(suffix)` (literal, empty prefix/suffix matches), plus the earlier `reverse` and `to-int`. The no-implicit-conversions law has one exception — the string-context Int exception: `+` concatenates when exactly one operand is `Int` and the other is `String` (the Int renders as `int.to-string` does, chains associate left to right, and two `Int` operands still add numerically), and `print` accepts an `Int` directly; `Bool` and every other type stay strict in these positions, and no other position converts. Lists compose through callback words taking ordinary function values: `list.map(values, transform)` (once per element left to right, fresh outer list, shared elements, source unchanged), `list.filter(values, predicate)` (keep matches), `list.select(values, predicate)` (keep the matches unmodified; visits every element, never short-circuits), `list.fold(values, initial, step)` (returns the final accumulator), `list.find(values, predicate)` (`Option.Some` first match or `Option.None`, empty list is `None`), `list.any(values, predicate)` (short-circuits `true` at the first match, empty is `false`), `list.all(values, predicate)` (short-circuits `false` at the first non-match, empty is `true`), `list.sort(values)` (stable ascending copy of `List<Int>`/`List<String>`, code-point string order, fresh outer list, source unchanged), and `list.sort-by(values, key)` (stable ascending copy ordered by an Int-or-String key callback evaluated once per element in source order before sorting); callbacks are explicit or word-name partials with no lambda syntax, may print or mutate unrelated values, cannot return a `Result` nor use one as a fold accumulator (`unhandled-result`), and the source list holds its `collection-iterating` traversal guard throughout. Arrays select whole rows: `array.select(values, predicate)` passes each row of a rank-2 array left to right as a fresh `List<T>`, keeps the rows whose `(List<T>) -> Bool` predicate holds unmodified (rectangle preserved, fresh outer array, zero rows when nothing matches), holds the source's traversal guard, and reports rank 3+ at runtime with `array.select requires a rank-2 array, found rank N` under the `array-rank` code. Lines build in a `Buffer`: `buffer.new()`, `buffer.add-line`, `buffer.line-count`, `buffer.line(i)` and `buffer.set-line(i, text)` (Results failing `buffer-range` on a bad index), `buffer.to-text`; `let` binds the buffer's name — two names observe one buffer — and `Buffer` is excluded from `==` and rejected by `print` (convert with `buffer.to-text`). Files read whole (`file.read(path)` to String) or streamed (`file.open(path)`, `file.read-line(f)` where end of file fails inside the Result, `file.close(f)` idempotent); `for line in file.stream(path)` streams chomped lines and guarantees the close on every exit, including loop-body failures. `file.write(contents, path, append = false)` writes text — contents first, then path; omitting `append` (or `false`) creates or truncates, `true` appends and creates a missing file; the trailing argument is a built-in constant default (calls may omit it, partials keep it deferred), no parent directory is created, the write is not atomic (a failure can leave a partial or truncated file), and the open/write/close stays inside the operation (no writable File escapes; created files 0644 before umask; symlinks followed). Path inspection: `file.list(folder)` returns a fresh `List<String>` of one folder level's bare entry names (not paths) in sorted order, dot entries included, inside `Result<List<String>, FileError>`, failing the shared `collection-limit` past one million entries before materializing; `file.exists(path)` is a plain `Bool` where a missing path is `false` and any other stat failure is a runtime diagnostic, with `try`/`catch` selecting the checked `Result<Bool, FileError>` form; `file.size(path)` returns a regular file's bytes (directories report `0`, no recursion) inside `Result<Int, FileError>`; `file.free-space(path)` accepts any existing path, file or folder, and returns the bytes available on its volume inside `Result<Int, FileError>` (Unix and Windows; other platforms fail inside the Result). Lexical path words compose and decompose without touching the disk, returning plain `String` (no Result, no `try`/`catch`): `file.join(base, child)` concatenates with the native separator and cleans (`..` resolves lexically, no containment guarantee) and an absolute child replaces the base (`file.join("a/b", "/c")` → `/c`); `file.base(path)` is the final element (trailing separators removed, the root is its own base, the empty path yields `.`); `file.extension(path)` is the final element's final-dot suffix including the dot (`.gz` for `report.tar.gz`, `.bashrc` for the dotfile, empty when absent); `file.directory-of(path)` drops the final element (a trailing separator leaves nothing to drop, the root is its own directory, no-drop yields `.`). Destructive operations return `Result<Unit, FileError>` with the same taxonomy: `file.make-folder(path, parents = false)` creates one folder level and fails on an existing target, while `parents = true` creates missing ancestors and tolerates an existing folder; `file.delete(path)` removes a file or an empty folder and fails on a nonempty one; `file.delete-folder(path, recursive = false)` removes an empty folder, and `recursive = true` removes the whole tree best-effort (part may be gone before the first failure; earlier effects stand); `file.move(source, target, overwrite = false)` is rename-based and moves folders as well as files, `overwrite = true` replaces an existing file only (folder targets are refused in both modes), cross-device moves fail with the platform's error with no copy fallback, and the target check and rename have a documented check-then-act window. File Results fail `file-open`, `file-read`, `file-write`, `file-utf8`, `file-list`, `file-exists`, `file-size`, `file-free-space`, `file-make-folder`, `file-delete`, `file-delete-folder`, or `file-move`, naming the path and the operating system's reason (`file-write` also names the failing phase: open, write, or close). Program arguments forward as `zhex run file.zhex [args...]`: read them with `console.args-count()` and `console.arg(i)` (a Result failing `argument-missing` on a bad index). Environment configuration reads the process environment: `env.get(name)` is a total `Option<String>` (unset is `Option.None`, set-but-empty is `Option.Some("")`; never a Result) and `env.load(path = ".env")` returns `Result<Unit, Error>` (common-Error family, the `json.parse` precedent), reading KEY=VALUE lines into the environment with first assignment wins — a key already in the environment, or set by an earlier line of the same file, is never overridden; blank lines and whole-line `#` comments are skipped after leading trim, one matching pair of surrounding single or double quotes on the value is stripped, `KEY=` sets the empty string, a read failure fails `env-read` and a malformed line (missing `=`, empty key, key with spaces) fails `env-parse` naming the line number, lines before a malformed one stay applied, and the `.env` trailing constant default stays deferred for partials like `file.write`'s `append`.
- Results and errors: built-ins return explicit `Result<T, E>`. Word parameter annotations may be omitted when body and same-program call constraints determine one concrete type; unresolved parameters need annotations, conflicting calls are type errors, and `Result` cannot be a word parameter. Trailing word parameters may have defaults; required parameters come first and calls remain positional. Defaults can infer parameter types, run lazily only when omitted, and evaluate after supplied arguments (source order) in parameter order. They use declaring-module scope, cannot reference parameters/globals/caller bindings or let a `Result` escape, and are fresh on each call; `words` displays `= ...`. Compatible REPL redefinitions affect new entries while checked callers retain the earlier word/defaults. Return annotations may also be omitted when the body determines one concrete success type. An escaping `try` infers one error family and the effective Result signature, and successful values are wrapped once. Pure words keep their inferred or annotated type. A recursive cycle without a concrete type anchor, empty collection, or nullary `Option.None` needs a return annotation. Explicit `Result<T, E>` signatures remain supported with `ok`/`err`, without wrapping twice. Each caller still uses `try` or `catch`; multiple uncaught families in one word are rejected, so catch a failure or explicitly wrap it as common `Error`. Runtime faults are not inferred. `catch [name]` lazily supplies a same-typed fallback or exits via `console.exit`/`console.fail`. Bare Results cannot be discarded; a stored `let pending = call()` must be handled by the immediately following same-block statement as exactly `pending try` or `pending catch ...`, standalone or as a whole new `let` RHS. Explicit flow steps use `word-name try`. `error.new` creates a cause-less application Error; `error.wrap` converts to common `Error` and preserves the cause; accessors include code/message/operation/file/line/column/detail/has-cause/cause. File detail `reason` values are `not-found`, `permission-denied`, `other` (open, write, and inspect), and `invalid-utf8`, `closed`, `read-failed`, `end-of-file` (read); a write failure's `detail` also carries its `phase`. `error.set-reporter(named-word)` installs a top-level `(Error) -> Unit` callback. `error.report(problem)` reports a handled occurrence; a failure escaping the program calls the reporter once before the diagnostic. Intermediate propagation does not report, duplicate occurrences are suppressed, callback failure/recursion is isolated, and no external destination is configured by default. `console.exit(status)` ends execution with 0..255, and `console.fail(message)` writes to stderr and ends with status 1; neither reports a valid deliberate exit. Out-of-range exit status is a runtime diagnostic. These exits close active `file.stream` loops; explicitly opened files still require `file.close`. Reporter calls to either operation cannot replace the original outcome.
- Modules: split a program across files with `use math` — it loads the sibling `math.zhex` next to the importing file (each file's own imports resolve beside it; the REPL resolves against the working directory and adopts the module for the session). Imported words are called qualified (`math.gcd(a, b)`); module words call each other bare inside their own file and cannot see the importer's words; a module's own imports stay private to it, and two modules never collide. A leading underscore makes a word or type module-private: calling one from outside fails `private-use`, and it is never suggested cross-module. A public signature, record field, or choice payload cannot expose a private type, even through a List, Array, Map, or Result. Imported choice constructors and cases are qualified (`model.Status.Ready`). Errors: a missing module fails `use-missing` naming the searched path; import cycles fail `use-cycle` spelling the files; module names `text`, `int`, `buffer`, `file`, `console`, `error`, `list`, `array`, `map`, `json`, `xml`, and `env` fail `use-reserved`; the built-in `Option` type and constructors are reserved names, but `Option` is not a reserved module name. Imported files may declare words and types but top-level statements fail `module-body`; `use` outside a file's top level fails `use-location` — and `use` is a reserved word. Loaded modules check before their importers, and module errors annotate the module's own source. Trace events carry qualified names (`{"word":"math.gcd"}`, module-private words included) with word returns pointing into the module file (`{"file":"math.zhex"}`). Corpus examples: `examples/modules/main.zhex` (math) and `examples/modules/md-report/main.zhex` (a pure-Zhex Markdown report module with `md.heading`, `md.paragraph`, `md.bullet-list`, `md.ordered-list`, `md.link`, `md.code-block`, and `md.table` — fragment-returning words with per-position escaping, `max(3, longest run + 1)` fences, strict header-width table rows, and neutralized `javascript:`/`data:` link schemes), each a two-file program run as `zhex run examples/<path>`.
- [Examples](https://desireco.github.io/zhex/examples.html): runnable programs with source, sample input, and real output — the source and output on the page are produced by the actual interpreter. The 22 in-subset examples also run in the visitor's browser — the build precompiles each to a WebAssembly artifact (WebAssembly garbage collection: roughly Chrome 119+, Firefox 120+, Safari 18.2+) that a page shim executes with the Go interpreter's byte-for-byte output, while the other 14 stay fenced with notes naming the construct the compiler does not cover yet. `text-stats` is the first real application: run it as `zhex run examples/text-stats.zhex <file> [upper]` — one argument reports the file's line, word, and character counts from one whole read, and any second argument streams the file uppercased line by line. `file-work` is the destructive round trip: run it as `zhex run examples/file-work.zhex <folder>` — it creates a zhex-work folder under the argument, writes and inspects two reports, and removes the tree. `env-config` is the configuration round trip: run it as `zhex run examples/env-config.zhex <folder>` — it writes a report.env fixture, loads it with first assignment wins, and reads each setting back through `env.get` Option matches. `collatz` shows the while loop: run it as `zhex run examples/collatz.zhex` — it prints each number's steps to reach 1, ending by its condition rather than a bound.
- [Demos](https://desireco.github.io/zhex/demos.html): Zhex programs running as themselves — the build compiles each demo to a WebAssembly artifact and the page replays the artifact's real stdout frame by frame (looping playback), currently one group, Game of Life, holding three runs: a Gosper glider gun, the acorn, and diehard.
- [Playground](https://desireco.github.io/zhex/playground.html): run and REPL in the browser over the real interpreter compiled to a WebAssembly engine — lazy-loaded behind the open click, with caret diagnostics in both modes, a stdin box, example preloading from the examples page cards, and share links carrying source, input, and mode in the URL fragment.
- [Advent of Code](https://desireco.github.io/zhex/advent-of-code.html): December 2025's twelve puzzles solved in Zhex — one door per day with the puzzle outline and the solution behind a details toggle (a browser run panel on the compiled days), year tabs with a teaser for the year in progress. The suites under `aoc/<year>/` run with `bin/zhex test aoc`, and the site build re-runs every door's browser artifact byte-for-byte against the interpreter.
- [Roadmap](https://desireco.github.io/zhex/roadmap.html): what is done, what is next, and what is future, mirrored by a public project board.
- [Changelog](https://desireco.github.io/zhex/changelog.html): every shipped milestone from the roadmap's Done section, grouped by area and generated from ROADMAP.md.
- [Error catalog](https://desireco.github.io/zhex/errors.html): built-in diagnostic codes with their meanings and fixes; application codes from `error.new`/`error.wrap` are not catalog entries. Diagnostics print `file:line:column: message` plus an excerpt, caret, and `hint:` line; `zhex run file.zhex --report=json` emits the machine-readable report `{code, severity, file, line, column, message, hint}`, plus optional additive span_start_column/span_end_column (checker diagnostics with a span, never runtime).
- [Development insight](https://github.com/desireco/zhex/blob/main/docs/diagnostics-plan.md): `zhex run file.zhex --trace` streams JSONL step events to stderr — one JSON object per line, emitted before any diagnostic, and combinable with `--report=json` (events, then the report). Four events: `{"event":"word-call","word":W,"file":F,"line":N,"args":[...]}`, `{"event":"binding","name":N,"value":V,"file":F,"line":N}`, `{"event":"flow-step","word":W,"value":V,"file":F,"line":N}`, `{"event":"word-return","word":W,"value":V,"file":F,"line":N}`. `word-call` fires only for program words — builtins never emit it; they appear as flow-step or binding effects. Bindings holding a `Result` (a read without postfix `try`) render `ok("inner")` or `err("message")`; other values render per the checker's static types — Int as digits, Bool as `true`/`false`, String verbatim, Unit as the empty string, Buffer as `buffer(<n> lines)`, File as `file("<path>")` — and a `-> Unit` word returns value "". Tracing never fails a run, and output without the flag is unchanged.
- REPL: `zhex repl [--trace]` runs an interactive session where words and values persist across entries; calls use parentheses (`print(1 + 1)`) or the simple comma-separated form (`print 1 + 1`). In a terminal, pending blocks prefill editable indentation; Tab inserts four spaces, Backspace removes one character; four presses dedent one level. An empty or spaces-only continuation line submits, except blank and comment-only lines inside open `()`, `[]`, or `{}`. Closing a completed top-level expression submits it immediately; a pending block still needs a blank line. While editing, Ctrl-C cancels the current entry; Ctrl-D on an empty top-level line exits 0; in a pending entry, an empty or spaces-only continuation line discards the entry and exits. Bracketed paste preserves source indentation. Piped entries retain line-based behavior and need explicit four-space block indentation; tabs and non-ASCII whitespace outside strings or comments remain source errors. An unclosed delimiter at piped EOF is a syntax error. Program `read-line` uses the same terminal reader without source auto-indentation or Tab expansion. Agents can script a session by piping entries to standard input. A blank line ends a multi-line entry when no delimiter is open; a missing indented block or open delimiter continues it. Bare ordinary expressions echo their value; naked Result expressions are rejected and must be handled with `try` or `catch` in the same entry. `words` lists effective parameter, return, and Result signatures sorted by name and shadows a user binding of that name; a word can be redefined with the same effective signature, while an incompatible signature change is rejected transactionally. Parameter inference must resolve within the defining entry. `let` shadows silently. Check and runtime errors print the annotated diagnostic and the session survives; a runtime error keeps the entry's earlier effects. A final input line without a trailing newline still runs. Ctrl-D or the preloaded ordinary REPL word `bye()` exits 0; the zero-argument call form `bye` is equivalent. `bye()` appears in `words`, follows normal redefinition rules, and is unavailable in source files. With `--trace`, the same JSONL step events as `zhex run` stream to stderr with `"file":"repl"`.

- [Standard library direction](https://desireco.github.io/zhex/docs/standard-library.html): current library boundaries and proposed growth. The [complete 114-name inventory and comparative research](https://github.com/desireco/zhex/blob/main/docs/standard-library-plan.md) distinguishes shipped operations from unimplemented draft stories; do not generate programs using proposed APIs.

## Reference

- [Language contract](https://github.com/desireco/zhex/blob/main/docs/initial-language.md): the authoritative syntax and semantics the interpreter enforces.
- [Versioning policy](https://github.com/desireco/zhex/blob/main/docs/versioning.md): no version numbers anywhere until the standard library's 0.1 release (main-only, no tags, no CHANGELOG before that); from 0.1, 0.x semver — MINOR for breaking changes, PATCH for additions — with git tags per release and a hand-written CHANGELOG.md; no release automation before 0.1.
- [Agent guide](https://github.com/desireco/zhex/blob/main/AGENTS.md): rules for writing correct Zhex and verifying changes with the executable test suite.
- [Example sources](https://desireco.github.io/zhex/examples/hello.zhex): downloadable `.zhex` files — swap the filename for fizzbuzz, fibonacci, gcd, times-table, factorial, palindrome, composition, calls, partials, records, choices, collections, maps, json-config, json-tree, xml-config, word-defaults, temporal, life, edit-distance, collatz, text-stats, line-filter, score-report, file-write, paths, file-work, env-config, recovery, or exit-status; the two-file module programs live at examples/modules/main.zhex with its math.zhex beside it and examples/modules/md-report/main.zhex with its md.zhex beside it, and the html composition module pairs the same way at examples/modules/html-page/main.zhex with its html.zhex (`html.escape-text`, `html.attr`, `html.element`, `html.page`, `html.raw` — escaped unless raw; `html.link` rejects any scheme besides relative, http, https, and mailto), and the module tests live at examples/modules/math.test.zhex with math.zhex and test.zhex beside it (`test.check(condition, label)` fails the run with its label when the condition is false; `zhex test [path]` runs every `*.test.zhex` file as its own process plus every other `.zhex` file's doctests, and `zhex test --gaps` lists public words referenced by no doctest and no test file).
- [Project board](https://github.com/users/desireco/projects/8): the backlog and delivered work as issues on a public Kanban board.
